---
title: "Posterior dependence and pairwise comparisons"
subtitle: "1.9 · two jointly normal posteriors; dependence after the postrank theory book, ch. 9 and 18"
description: "Effect of correlation on direction probabilities under a bivariate normal posterior distribution."
---

Two units can have the same marginal posterior distributions under different assumptions about how their true values move together. In a bivariate normal posterior, positive correlation reduces the variance of A − B, while negative correlation increases it. The shaded region below the equality line gives $\pi_{AB}$, and the ellipse encloses .90 of the joint posterior probability. The first example holds the marginal distributions and the mean difference fixed as correlation changes. The probability can move closer to or farther from one half, with the same direction remaining more probable. A second example obtains the correlation from uncertainty about a shared prior mean.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Correlation .50.** The ellipse follows the equality line because the two true values move together. The difference has SD .200, compared with .283 under independence, and $\pi_{AB}$ = .841 against .760.
- **Independent.** Correlation 0 with equal SDs draws a circle: the difference has SD .283, and $\pi_{AB}$ = .760.
- **Correlation .95.** Strong positive dependence gives a difference with SD .063, and $\pi_{AB}$ = .999.
- **Correlation −.95.** The ellipse lies across the line, and the difference widens to SD .395: $\pi_{AB}$ falls to
  .694, toward one half, not past it.
- **Shared prior mean.** Estimates .30 and .10 with SEs .20; true values spread with SD .10 around an uncertain prior
  mean (SD .50). The model gives correlation .645, SD .126 for the difference and $\pi_{AB}$ = .624; assuming independence for the same marginals gives .212 and .575. With prior-mean SD set to 0, the correlation vanishes, each posterior narrows to SD .089, and $\pi_{AB}$ stays .624.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Where the correlation comes from.** Given the prior mean, each posterior mean keeps the share
$k = \text{prior SD}^2/(\text{prior SD}^2 + \text{SE}^2)$ of its estimate, independently. Both posterior variables depend on the uncertain prior mean, so their covariance is $(1 - k_A)(1 - k_B)\,v$, with $v$ the prior mean's variance given both
estimates (theory book, ch. 18); with equal SEs the shared part cancels from the difference. postrank takes such
posteriors as joint draws, or as normal laws averaged over the prior mean (`postrank_mixture_coefficients()`).
:::

Standalone: [embed/correlated-units.html](../../embed/correlated-units.html), for example `?corr=-.50` or
`?preset=shared-mean&meanSd=0`.

Related applications: [Pairwise posterior direction probabilities](two-units.qmd) (1.8) works the independent case;
[Marginal summaries and joint direction probabilities](beyond-normal.qmd) (1.10) drops joint normality: there the means no longer fix
the side of one half.
